quantities: Per-channel electron temperature and supported flow projection from measured full spectra; absolute electron density where identifiable; joint channel-to-channel covariance for non-collective Maxwellian/Kappa models when a full spectral covariance is supplied; collective-mode external-parameter and response uncertainty propagation by Monte Carlo when supplied.
method: Forward-fit measured, calibrated multi-channel Thomson spectra using a required measured instrument-response callable/kernel/matrix. Supports non-collective Maxwellian, non-collective kappa, projected relativistic Maxwell-Juttner and optional PlasmaPy collective Maxwellian dielectric inference with explicit ion species, fractions, ion temperatures and flow vectors. Absolute non-collective density requires W/nm spectral intensity plus laser power, interaction length, collection solid angle, optical efficiency and complete polarized beam geometry.
caveat: Collective-mode ion temperatures and ion/electron flow vectors remain externally supplied, not fitted. Supplied uncertainties and measured response-matrix uncertainty are propagated by Monte Carlo when supplied; beam-direction component uncertainties are independent and cross-source correlations are not represented. Joint full-covariance GLS supports non-collective Maxwellian and Kappa only. The relativistic option remains a 1-D projected approximation. No independent experimental validation is claimed.
implementation_status: Canonical measured-calibrated-spectrum physical inference supports non-collective Maxwellian, Kappa, projected Maxwell-Juttner and optional PlasmaPy collective Maxwellian models; full channel-major GLS for Maxwellian/Kappa; Monte Carlo propagation of supplied collective beam-geometry, flow, ion-temperature, laser-wavelength and response uncertainties; absolute-density recomputation after joint fitting; and separate model-discrepancy diagnostics. Optional full 6N x 6N density-input covariance preserves cross-channel correlations in absolute electron-density outputs.

assumptions: Input spectra and wavelength axes are measured and calibrated; calibration is not performed by Analysis 1.
Spatial coordinates are supplied for each measured channel.
Non-collective Maxwellian model assumes isotropic non-relativistic Maxwellian electrons.
Collective Maxwellian model requires explicit ion species and ion temperatures; missing values are not silently inferred.
Absolute density requires W/nm spectral intensity and complete optical geometry/polarization inputs.
Collective-mode flow vectors and incident/scattered beam directions are expressed in one explicitly supplied coordinate frame; no canonical beam orientation is assumed.
preprocessing: Validate finite channel-by-wavelength arrays, channel-to-radius correspondence and strictly increasing calibrated wavelength axes without sorting, repairing or dropping source samples.

Apply the supplied instrument response in bin-integrated spectral-power space using calibrated wavelength-bin widths, then convert back to spectral density; 1-D index kernels require a uniform wavelength grid.
execution_contract.algorithm: Forward-fit measured multi-channel Thomson spectra with the supplied instrument response. Infer per-channel electron temperature and supported flow projection; infer collective-mode density only where the collective spectral shape resolves it, and non-collective absolute density only when calibrated spectral power and complete optical geometry are supplied.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Non-collective fits use local fit covariance and optional Monte Carlo LSF uncertainty. A full channel-major covariance is handled by joint GLS for Maxwellian/Kappa and final physical parameters, integrated powers and absolute densities are recomputed from the joint fit. Collective external-parameter Monte Carlo includes supplied ion-temperature, ion/electron flow-vector, laser-wavelength, scattering-angle or beam-direction component, and measured response-matrix uncertainties; the returned covariance includes channel density, temperature and projected flow parameters. A supplied 6x6 relative optical-input covariance is authoritative and mutually exclusive with separate scalar uncertainty inputs. Excess reduced chi-square is exposed as a separate model-adequacy covariance diagnostic, not experimental validation. Optional joint_density_relative_covariance provides a complete 6N x 6N channel-major covariance for absolute-density inversion and returns the full cross-channel density covariance; it cannot be combined with joint_spectral_covariance or separate response/scalar optical uncertainty models.
limitations: Full 3-D relativistic photon-geometry integration is not implemented; the relativistic option uses a 1-D projected Maxwell-Juttner approximation.
Collective non-Maxwellian kinetic distributions are not implemented; the collective backend is Maxwellian.
The kappa model is a parameterized isotropic non-Maxwellian approximation, not arbitrary VDF inversion.
Absolute density is not identifiable from spectral shape alone.
No independent experimental validation is claimed.
Collective multi-species inference requires explicit ion composition fractions; ion temperatures and flow vectors must be supplied or stationary assumptions declared.
Collective-mode fitting requires explicit incident/scattered beam direction vectors consistent with the supplied scattering angle.
Joint full-covariance GLS is currently implemented for non-collective Maxwellian and Kappa projected spectra; other models require dedicated joint forward models.
Model-discrepancy covariance uses excess reduced chi-square as a conditional diagnostic and is not a substitute for independent model validation.

Collective beam-direction component uncertainties are propagated as independent component-wise Gaussian perturbations; correlations among beam-vector components and correlations with other external inputs are not represented.
A supplied density_relative_covariance is authoritative for all six optical inversion inputs, including the scattered-power uncertainty; do not also supply separate scalar uncertainties.
execution_contract.note: Primary Analysis 1 accepts measured, calibrated multi-channel Thomson spectra and infers physical parameters. Legacy profile-summary/interpolation helpers are compatibility utilities only and are not registered or exposed as diagnostic workflows.

quantities: Calibrated I–V sweeps; floating potential and conditional uncertainty; maximum-dI/dV proxy and second-derivative zero-crossing candidates; single-/two-temperature empirical fits; stretched-exponential shape comparison; electron temperature; model-based electron/ion density and ion particle flux; multispecies density with number-density fractions; independent multi-channel/time batches; fit-window sensitivity and explicitly parameterized smoothing.
method: Analyze already-calibrated single-probe I–V data with explicit current polarity and disjoint analyst-selected electron/ion fit windows. Report maximum-dI/dV as a proxy and second-derivative zero crossings as separate inflection candidates; retain the second-derivative maximum only as a distinct extremum. Numerical fit screens are identical across engine and UI. Optional density/flux outputs use published Maxwellian collection and sheath/Bohm relations with explicitly supplied geometry, species and model coefficients.
caveat: All inputs are assumed calibrated and correctly organized. Numerical candidates and model estimates are not confirmed measurements; physical regimes are never automatically certified. Grid spacing is resolution only. Current-noise uncertainty is conditional on supplied per-sample standard uncertainty. Missing/invalid fit covariance is reported as unavailable, never zero. Number-density fractions are required for multispecies inversion. No empirical validation is claimed.
implementation_status: Canonical calibrated single-sweep workflow plus UI-accessible advanced models, density/flux estimates and independent channel/time batch workflows. All advanced fits normalize current polarity to electron_positive, report covariance-based component uncertainties and identifiability diagnostics where available, and explicitly avoid physical-regime certification. Multispecies fractions are number-density fractions. No calibration or empirical validation is performed.

assumptions: Voltage and current are calibrated and synchronized samples from a quasi-static single-probe I–V sweep.
The electron-retarding branch is adequately described by an exponential current after fitting its offset.
Fit intervals are selected and justified by the analyst for the experimental regime.
Density inversion assumes one dominant ion species and requires a supplied coefficient appropriate to the stated sheath model, probe geometry and plasma regime.
Multi-channel batch mode treats each calibrated channel independently and does not infer spatial relationships or shared physical regimes.
Current standard uncertainty, when supplied, represents independent per-original-sample 1-sigma errors; Monte Carlo proxy uncertainty is conditional on that model.
Single-species ion density uses explicit integer charge state Z_i; default Z_i=1 is a declared singly charged assumption, and Bohm speed scales as sqrt(Z_i e T_e/m_i).
preprocessing: Require matching one-dimensional voltage/current arrays and at least eight valid distinct voltage points across all public Langmuir entry points.
Discard non-finite pairs; sort voltage-current pairs together; average currents at duplicate voltages.
Use explicit analyst-selected fit windows; no automatic physical regime selection.
Report input pair count, finite-pair count, discarded non-finite pairs, duplicate-voltage pairs aggregated, processed unique voltages, voltage span and normalized current convention.
When a scalar per-sample current standard uncertainty is supplied, propagate it through duplicate-voltage averaging using independent-error averaging; no uncertainty is assumed when omitted.
execution_contract.algorithm: Normalize the selected current polarity to electron_positive; clean calibrated I–V pairs; aggregate duplicate voltages with corresponding uncertainty reduction; compute floating-potential crossings; compute dI/dV and d²I/dV²; report maximum dI/dV as a proxy, zero crossings of d²I/dV² as inflection candidates, and maximum d²I/dV² only as a separate extremum. Require disjoint analyst-selected fit windows; apply identical numerical fit screens in the engine and UI; by default gate density inversion on both electron and ion numerical fit quality and ion flatness, with an explicit opt-in override that marks any resulting density provisional; retain all physical-regime flags as unconfirmed. Advanced functions use explicitly declared published models and independent channel/time batching. Advanced fits share canonical finite-pair filtering, polarity normalization, sorting and duplicate-voltage averaging. Smoothed derivatives use local polynomial least squares in actual voltage coordinates, not a uniform-sample Savitzky-Golay assumption.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Canonical Te and single-species density uncertainties use only valid fit covariance and explicitly supplied independent components. Electron-density and Bohm-flux helpers propagate only when all required uncertainties are supplied. Multispecies density now supports partial independent propagation from explicitly supplied ion-current, Te, area, species-mass and species-sheath-coefficient uncertainties; omitted terms, especially constrained number-fraction covariance, are listed and never silently set to zero. Stretched-exponential errors are conditional empirical-fit covariance errors. Invalid covariance yields null.
limitations: Saturation-tail estimates are descriptive fallbacks and cannot be used for density inversion.
Density requires an explicitly justified sheath coefficient, collection area, ion mass, and both physically selected fit windows.
Single-ion-species assumption; mixtures require an appropriate model or separate treatment.
Plasma-potential output is a dI/dV proxy, not a universally valid Vp measurement.
Check fit quality and probe-specific magnetic-field, RF, collision, secondary-emission, surface and sweep-direction effects.
The dI/dV maximum is a plasma-potential proxy, not a universally valid plasma-potential measurement.

Canonical ion density is a model-based estimate requiring explicit fit-window, geometry, ion-mass and sheath-model inputs; advanced particle-flux estimates use an explicit Bohm-like model and supplied density.
Numerical fit screening cannot certify electron-retarding or ion-saturation physical regimes.
Density inversion is refused when the selected ion interval fails numerical fit-quality or flatness screening; passing this screen does not confirm physical ion saturation.
Density uncertainty propagation is partial and includes only explicitly supplied uncertainty components.
The maximum dI/dV voltage is a proxy only; physical plasma potential requires regime-specific justification.
Canonical single-sweep analysis does not infer probe geometry or cross-channel physics; explicit array and time-series helpers process sweeps independently.
Maximum dI/dV and maximum d2I/dV2 are candidate indicators only; neither universally determines physical plasma potential.
Voltage-grid spacing is a resolution indicator, not a statistical uncertainty.
Ion-current estimates are explicitly labelled and do not automatically certify the physical ion-saturation regime.
Te and density uncertainty propagation includes only fit statistics and explicitly supplied components; missing systematic components are not inferred.
Multi-channel batch processing does not provide spatial reconstruction, cross-channel correlation, or multi-probe geometry inference.
The two-temperature fit is an empirical two-exponential mixture; the stretched-exponential helper is an empirical shape comparison, not a kinetic kappa-distribution model.

Advanced multispecies density propagates only explicitly supplied independent current, Te, area, species-mass and sheath-coefficient uncertainties; species number-fraction covariance is excluded and reported.
Two-temperature fitting is an empirical two-exponential decomposition and does not confirm a physical bi-Maxwellian distribution.
Time-series batching processes each time/channel sweep independently and does not infer temporal trends or cross-channel physics.
Fit-window sensitivity is a diagnostic spread, not a statistical confidence interval.
Electron-density estimation is available only through the separate estimate_electron_density_from_saturation helper and is not part of the canonical single-sweep output contract.
The second-derivative zero-crossing method is noise-sensitive; candidate locations depend on differentiation, smoothing choice and voltage sampling.
Monte Carlo uncertainty for the maximum-dI/dV proxy is conditional on supplied independent current errors and is not an uncertainty for the true physical plasma potential.
Numerical R², NRMSE and ion-flatness thresholds are configurable screening parameters, not universal physical acceptance criteria.
Multispecies density includes species charge state through Z_s^(3/2); species composition covariance is not propagated.
Local polynomial smoothing fits in actual voltage coordinates and supports nonuniform voltage spacing; smoothing window is specified in sample count.
Time-series output preserves time_labels and channel_names but does not compute temporal derivatives, trends, correlations, or spatial reconstruction.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated shared or channel-specific voltage/current sweeps; explicit optional fit and polarity options.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Independent per-channel canonical results; no cross-channel inference, spatial reconstruction or geometry inference.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: analysis_scope, channel_count, channels mapping each channel name to a canonical single-sweep result, cross_channel_inference_performed=false.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated current array shaped (time, channel, sample), with shared or matching calibrated voltage data and optional time/channel labels.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Independent per-time/per-channel sweep results; no temporal trend or cross-channel inference.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated voltage/current arrays, explicit fit range, model choice and current_convention (electron_positive or ion_positive); current is normalized internally to electron_positive. Shared canonical preprocessing filters non-finite pairs, sorts and averages duplicate voltages; requires at least eight distinct voltages globally and model-specific distinct points in fit interval. Two-temperature mode is an empirical two-exponential decomposition, not proof of two populations.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Temperature component estimates and fit diagnostics; physical distribution is not confirmed.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Merlino (2007), American Journal of Physics 75, 1078-1085, DOI: 10.1119/1.2772282, Appendix Problem 1; Stangeby (1984), Journal of Nuclear Materials 128-129, 969-973, DOI: 10.1016/0022-3115(84)90496-3. Two-temperature decomposition is conditional on two Maxwellian components and fit identifiability.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: model_class and physical_interpretation_status; electron_temperature_components_eV; covariance validity, parameter standard errors and component temperature standard uncertainties when covariance is valid; all uncertainty outputs null with explicit status when covariance is invalid; physical_distribution_confirmed is always false.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated voltage/current arrays, explicit fit range and current_convention (electron_positive or ion_positive); current is normalized internally to electron_positive. Shared canonical preprocessing filters non-finite pairs, sorts and averages duplicate voltages; covariance-derived parameter errors are conditional on empirical curve-shape model and fit window. Uses the mirrored KWW increasing-branch form I(V)=I0+A exp(-[s(V_ref-V)]^beta), with V_ref fixed to the selected fit-window upper endpoint; V_ref is not a plasma-potential estimate.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Empirical shape exponent and fit diagnostics; not a kinetic kappa distribution.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Williams and Watts (1970), Transactions of the Faraday Society 66, 80-85, DOI: 10.1039/TF9706600080, for the generic empirical KWW shape only. This implementation is a mirrored empirical curve-shape fit, not a Langmuir-probe theory relation or a physical EEDF model.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: empirical model_class; fit parameters and fit quality; covariance-derived parameter_standard_errors and shape_exponent_standard_uncertainty only when covariance is valid, otherwise null with parameter_uncertainty_status; kinetic_distribution_identified is false. Returns reference_voltage_V as the selected fit-window upper endpoint, never as an inferred plasma potential.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Ion saturation current, positive Te and area, and per-species masses, positive integer charge states Z_s, number-density fractions and sheath coefficients; fractions sum to one. Optional absolute current sigma, relative Te/area sigma, and per-species relative mass/sheath-coefficient sigmas are accepted. Fractions are treated as fixed; fraction uncertainty is rejected unless a future composition covariance model is implemented.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Model-based total ion density and partial uncertainty from explicitly supplied independent components; omitted terms and the exclusion of composition covariance are reported.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Species-summed extension of the species-resolved Bohm/sheath current balance described by Hutchinson (2002), Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5. The Z_s^(3/2) dependence follows from multiplying species charge Z_s e by the species Bohm speed sqrt(Z_s e T_e/m_s); applicability of each sheath coefficient remains an explicit user assumption.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: ion_density_estimate_m-3; partial ion_density_standard_uncertainty_m-3 and relative uncertainty only when at least one explicit independent uncertainty is supplied; uncertainty components and omitted components are listed; species fraction covariance is excluded; no uncertainty inputs yields null uncertainty and explicit status.
advanced_entry_points.uncertainty_model: Independent first-order propagation: current, area and temperature terms plus species-weighted sheath-coefficient and mass terms. Species number fractions are held fixed because their sum constraint requires a composition covariance model; missing terms are reported as omitted, not zero-filled.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Positive electron-saturation current, electron temperature, and effective collection area. Optional uncertainty propagation requires absolute current σ and relative Te/area σ; otherwise uncertainty is null with explicit status. Reference: Hutchinson (2002), Ch. 3, §3.2.5.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Separate helper result: electron_density_estimate_m-3, explicit Maxwellian collection formula and assumptions, physical_regime_confirmed=false, uncertainty_propagation_performed=false. Not a field automatically generated by analyze_langmuir_probe.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Merlino (2007), American Journal of Physics 75, 1078-1085, Eq. (6), DOI: 10.1119/1.2772282; Hutchinson (2002), Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: electron_density_estimate_m-3; standard uncertainty only when absolute current sigma and relative Te and area sigmas are all supplied, otherwise null with status; physical_regime_confirmed is false.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Ion density, electron temperature, ion mass, and explicitly supplied sheath factor. Explicit positive integer charge state Z_i; optional uncertainty propagation requires all four relative input uncertainties (density, Te, mass, sheath factor). Bohm speed sqrt(Z_i e T_e/m_i).
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Separate helper result: Bohm-like sound speed and particle-flux estimate under supplied inputs; uncertainty_propagation_performed=false. Not inferred from multi-channel or time-series batching.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Merlino (2007), American Journal of Physics 75, 1078-1085, Eq. (3), DOI: 10.1119/1.2772282; Hutchinson (2002), Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: ion_sound_speed_m_s, ion_particle_flux_m-2_s-1 and explicit integer charge_state; flux standard uncertainty only when all four relative uncertainties are supplied, otherwise null with status.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated voltage/current arrays and explicit odd local window point count and polynomial order. Local polynomial least squares uses actual voltage coordinates and supports nonuniform grids; raw and smoothed candidates remain separate.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Raw-gradient and local-polynomial-smoothed derivative candidates, separate maximum-d²I/dV² extrema and zero-crossing inflection candidates; local fits use actual voltage coordinates, including nonuniform grids.
advanced_entry_points.reference: Fan and Gijbels (1996), Local Polynomial Modelling and Its Applications, for local polynomial smoothing in actual voltage coordinates.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: raw and locally smoothed dI/dV and d2I/dV2 candidates, zero crossings, smoothing metadata and input-quality metadata; local polynomial method uses actual nonuniform voltage coordinates; no physical plasma potential is certified.

advanced_entry_points.input_contract: Calibrated voltage/current arrays, reference fit range, and optional relative shifts.
advanced_entry_points.outputs: Temperature spread across alternative windows; not a statistical confidence interval.
advanced_entry_points.output_contract: Base and caller-specified alternative fit-window results, fitted electron-temperature estimates, observed spread/sensitivity and per-window fit diagnostics. The spread is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a statistical confidence interval or a physical-regime validation.

execution_contract.note: Analysis uses already-calibrated single-probe I–V samples. The canonical output contract covers the single-sweep pipeline; optional ion density is part of that pipeline and requires explicit fit windows and physical inputs. Electron density and particle flux are separate advanced helper calls with their own explicit inputs and outputs, not canonical single-sweep output fields. All public entry points share the canonical implementation where applicable. Fit-window diagnostics are numerical screening only and do not certify physical regimes. Uncertainty propagation includes only explicitly supplied components; other systematics are not inferred. Synthetic tests are software regression checks, not experimental validation.
completion_criteria: Canonical output keys are covered by the diagnostic registry output_specs and tested for contract parity.
Current polarity is normalized consistently across canonical and advanced public functions.
Electron and ion fit windows are disjoint; density inversion requires both electron and ion numerical fit screens to pass.
All model-based density and flux estimates retain explicit assumptions and physical_regime_confirmed=false.
Advanced single-/two-temperature, stretched-exponential, smoothing, sensitivity, multispecies, array and series helpers are accessible through the public module and application UI.
Software tests verify numerical contracts; no empirical validation is claimed.
All advanced fit paths share canonical duplicate aggregation and minimum distinct-voltage requirements.
Numerical fit thresholds are configurable, exposed in result metadata and never described as physical-regime certification.
Ion charge state is explicit in single- and multi-species Bohm/sheath density models.
Advanced helper uncertainty fields are propagated only when all required independent uncertainty inputs are supplied; otherwise null/status is explicit.
Registry documents all supported single-sweep, multi-channel mapping/array and time-by-channel input shapes and labels.

numerical_screening.meaning: Numerical fit-quality and flatness screens only. Defaults are software review settings, not universal physical criteria, not plasma constants and never certify a Maxwellian electron-retarding or ion-saturation regime.
numerical_screening.density_gate: By default density inversion requires electron and ion fits to pass configured numerical review screens. These screens are not physical-regime criteria. The caller may explicitly set allow_density_when_numerical_screen_fails=true to obtain a provisional calculation from available fitted values; the output marks ion_density_numerical_screen_override_used=true and physical_regime_confirmed remains false. A missing or invalid Te/current still prevents calculation.

Mapping containing counts and ordered time_slices; each slice preserves the supplied time label and maps channel names to canonical single-sweep results. No temporal interpolation, derivatives, trends, or cross-channel inference are performed.

note: Canonical calibrated single-sweep I–V analysis with consistent public entry points and optional explicit sheath-model ion-density inversion. No geometry or sheath coefficient is silently inferred. Completion is scoped to the documented software contract and does not imply independent experimental validation.
references: Hutchinson, I. H., Principles of Plasma Diagnostics, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2002), Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5, Eqs. 3.2.33–3.2.37.

Hutchinson, I. H., Principles of Plasma Diagnostics, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2002), Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5 (Maxwellian electron collection and Bohm/sheath ion flux relations).

quantities: ECE resonance mapping, calibrated brightness temperature, inferred radial electron-temperature profile under declared assumptions, channel fluctuations and spectra
method: Five ECE workflows: calibrated radiance to Rayleigh–Jeans brightness temperature; cold or optional monoenergetic relativistic/Doppler resonance sensitivity; simplified circular-field, supplied monotonic Bphi(R), or explicit channel-radius mapping; receiver-response convolution with a supplied kernel; multi-channel RMS/periodogram/Welch PSD, cross-spectra/coherence and stationarity diagnostics; time-windowed PCHIP/linear Te profile reconstruction with optional uncertainty propagation.
caveat: Brightness temperature approximates electron temperature only for optically thick, thermalized emission. Radius mapping remains one-dimensional and is not full EFIT flux-coordinate mapping or line-of-sight ray tracing. The monoenergetic relativistic/Doppler correction is a sensitivity estimate, not distribution-averaged emissivity. Receiver convolution uses the supplied response kernel and measured spectral coverage; it does not infer calibration or perform radiative-transfer inversion. Profile uncertainties are approximate first-order estimates; covariance and temporal autocorrelation are included only when supplied/selected, and unknown model discrepancy remains unquantified. Cross spectra/coherence do not identify modes automatically. No experimental validation is implied.
implementation_status: Complete within declared software scope: calibrated-input brightness-temperature calculations, optional monoenergetic resonance sensitivity correction, 1-D simplified or supplied Bphi(R)/explicit-radius mapping, supplied receiver-response convolution, channel cross-spectral statistics, stationarity heuristics, PCHIP/linear profile reconstruction, first-order uncertainty propagation with optional channel covariance/autocorrelation/radial-gradient terms, and optional user-selected model-discrepancy floor. Inputs are already calibrated; no detector calibration is performed. Full EFIT/ray tracing, distribution-averaged relativistic emissivity, radiative-transfer inversion and inference of missing receiver response remain outside scope.

assumptions: Frequencies and calibrated radiance/brightness-temperature values are supplied in the documented SI/eV units; TIS performs no detector calibration.
Brightness temperature approximates Te only under appropriate optical-depth, thermalization and propagation assumptions.
Cold resonance mapping is the default; the optional monoenergetic relativistic/Doppler term is only a sensitivity estimate.
Radial localization is approximate unless the user supplies validated channel resonance positions; a monotonic Bphi(R) table is still not full ray tracing.
Fluctuation analysis requires finite approximately uniformly sampled signals; acquisition synchronization and anti-aliasing remain user responsibilities.
Profile and PSD uncertainty estimates are approximate; optional covariance/autocorrelation/model-discrepancy terms are included only when supplied, and unknown discrepancy remains unquantified.
preprocessing: Validate positive channel frequencies, paired channel selection, finite synchronized samples, monotonic time, sampling uniformity and optional uncertainty shapes; do not silently discard invalid rows.
For fluctuations, subtract per-channel mean, report sampling and Nyquist frequencies, full-record periodogram, Welch PSD confidence bounds and optional white-noise PSD reference.
For profile reconstruction, use already-calibrated brightness-temperature samples, select a valid time window, and supply optical depth or explicitly assert the optically thick approximation.
Sort channel frequencies and their associated measurements/uncertainties together. Report bandwidth-derived radial localization envelopes where bandwidth is supplied.
execution_contract.algorithm: Compute cold or optional monoenergetic relativistic/Doppler-sensitivity harmonic resonance fields and optional simplified circular-field, supplied monotonic Bphi(R), or explicit channel-radius mapping. Convert already-calibrated spectral radiance to Rayleigh–Jeans brightness temperature. Convolve a supplied calibrated spectrum with a user-supplied receiver response kernel using in-range linear interpolation and trapezoidal integration. For fluctuations compute RMS, a full-record one-sided periodogram, Hann-window Welch PSD with 50% overlap, approximate chi-square confidence bounds, sampling audit, spectral candidates, pairwise cross-spectra/coherence/phase and optional white-noise reference. For profiles, average already-calibrated brightness-temperature samples over a selected time window, infer Te using supplied single-slab optical depth or explicit optically-thick assumption, propagate optional measurement uncertainty/covariance/autocorrelation/radial-gradient terms, report bandwidth-derived radial localization envelope, and interpolate only within measured approximate resonance radii.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Welch PSD confidence intervals use approximate effective degrees of freedom for overlapping segments. Profile uncertainty uses first-order propagation for supplied brightness-temperature, optical-depth, background, frequency, reference-radius and field uncertainties; optional channel covariance and temporal-autocorrelation adjustment are included when supplied/selected. A user-specified model-discrepancy floor is optional and does not quantify unknown discrepancy. Bandwidth-derived radial envelopes are localization bounds, not statistical confidence intervals.
limitations: No detector calibration, inferred receiver response, full radiative-transfer inversion, automatic EFIT equilibrium, full line-of-sight ray tracing, polarization/cutoff solver, or distribution-averaged relativistic/Doppler emissivity.
Circular-field radius and monotonic Bphi(R) inversion are one-dimensional estimates, not flux-surface coordinates or a substitute for validated viewing geometry.
Brightness temperature is not automatically electron temperature; optical depth alone does not prove thermalization.

Receiver-response convolution requires a user-supplied validated kernel and complete spectral coverage; reported channel brightness temperature uses the response-weighted center frequency and is approximate for broad channels.
Welch confidence bounds are approximate and rely on the stated segment model; the stationarity check is heuristic. Supplied white-noise PSD is a reference and is not subtracted.
Radial profiles are interpolation-based, not a regularized radiative-transfer inversion. Finite bandwidth is a localization envelope, not a full response convolution.
Uncertainty estimates are first-order. Missing covariance, calibration uncertainty and unknown model discrepancy remain unquantified; low optical depth can make inversion ill-conditioned.
All radiance and brightness-temperature inputs must already be calibrated before import.
execution_contract.note: The dashboard and Python API execute four ECE workflows: calibrated-radiance brightness temperature, resonance mapping, multi-channel fluctuation/periodogram/Welch PSD, and time-windowed profile reconstruction with optional uncertainty, bandwidth-envelope and time-resolved outputs. Inputs must already be calibrated; no detector calibration is performed. Approximate model outputs are not experimental validation.

execution_contract.algorithm: Fit Gaussian emission plus local linear background using nonlinear least squares. Compute intrinsic Doppler sigma from sqrt(sigma_observed^2 - sigma_instrument^2), Ti = m_i c^2/e * (sigma_D/lambda_0)^2, and v_los = c*(lambda_center-lambda_0)/lambda_0. Propagate local fit covariance to Ti and line-of-sight velocity uncertainties. The declared completion boundary is calibrated isolated-line inference only; no uncalibrated detector-to-physics claim is made.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Local nonlinear least-squares covariance; optional per-sample standard deviations enable weighted fitting. First-order ion-temperature uncertainty includes observed-width fit covariance, optional independent instrumental-width uncertainty, and optional independent rest-wavelength uncertainty. Line-of-sight velocity uncertainty includes line-center covariance and optional rest-wavelength uncertainty. Assumes independent uncertainty contributions; excludes wavelength-axis calibration, ion-mass, covariance and model/systematic discrepancy.
limitations: No atomic-rate or neutral-beam attenuation model and no impurity-density estimate.
No toroidal/poloidal rotation inversion; reported velocity is line-of-sight only.
No line deblending, opacity correction, non-Maxwellian distribution, or non-Gaussian instrumental response.
Viewing angle is metadata only and does not perform geometric deprojection.
Covariance-based errors omit calibration and model systematics; independent experimental validation remains required.

assumptions: Wavelength axis is calibrated and the rest transition and ion species are correctly identified.
The feature is an isolated Gaussian emission line over a locally linear background.
Instrumental and thermal Doppler profiles are Gaussian and independent, permitting quadrature width subtraction.
Nonthermal flow distributions and Stark, Zeeman, opacity, unresolved blend/fine-structure broadening are negligible or separately corrected.
preprocessing: Reject nonfinite, mismatched, non-1D, too-short, or non-increasing wavelength arrays.
Require positive rest wavelength and ion mass; the rest wavelength must fall within the measured wavelength window.
Validate finite nonnegative instrumental width and positive finite per-sample intensity uncertainties when supplied.
Reject flat/no-contrast spectra and emission peaks at the spectral-window boundary.
Fit a Gaussian amplitude and center with positive sigma plus linear local background; convert fit failures and nonphysical fit parameters into clear validation errors.
Reject fitted centers at the wavelength-window boundary, excessively broad fits, and unresolved widths when observed FWHM does not exceed instrumental FWHM.
execution_contract.algorithm: Fit an isolated line to a Gaussian with linear background. Reject out-of-window rest wavelengths, boundary-truncated peaks/centers, failed/nonphysical fits and line widths too broad for the selected window. Convert fitted sigma to observed FWHM, deconvolve known Gaussian instrumental FWHM in quadrature, then calculate Ti using Ti[eV] = (mi c^2/e) (FWHM_D/lambda0)^2/(8 ln 2). Return fitted spectrum, residuals, fit covariance, R-squared and assumptions.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: When intensity uncertainties are supplied, use weighted nonlinear least squares with absolute sigma. Otherwise use the fitter's residual-scaled covariance. Propagate observed-width and instrumental-width uncertainty to Ti by first-order independent-error propagation when both are available. Excludes wavelength calibration, ion-mass, instrument-model and physical-model discrepancy.
limitations: Not a general Voigt, Stark/Zeeman, opacity, unresolved multiplet or non-Maxwellian line-shape solver.
Fit quality metrics do not prove that the fitted width is thermal.
Instrument width must correspond to the same wavelength, spectrometer configuration, slit/grating and optical path.
Near the instrumental-resolution limit, Ti and its uncertainty become poorly identifiable; unresolved widths are rejected.
Temperature uncertainty excludes systematic wavelength calibration, rest-wavelength, mass, calibration and model uncertainties.

limitations: Spectral moments characterize the measured wavelength distribution and are not a unique electron velocity distribution.
The descriptive moment routine does not independently infer electron temperature or density; those quantities come from the canonical physical-inference workflow.
The spectral-edge background fallback can remove real signal when the physical spectrum extends into the selected edge samples; a background-only mask is preferred.
A general measured response matrix is used for the Gaussian forward-fit diagnostic, but scalar Gaussian variance deconvolution is not claimed for a general non-Gaussian response.
Monte Carlo moment uncertainty excludes correlated wavelength-bin noise and shared calibration/systematic uncertainty.
Kappa is a parameterized projection rather than arbitrary VDF inversion; projected Maxwell-Juttner is a 1-D approximation; collective Maxwellian requires external ion parameters.
Moment uncertainties are descriptive spectral-moment uncertainties only and must not be interpreted as complete physical-parameter uncertainties.
execution_contract.note: This entry delegates measured-spectrum physical inference to the canonical Thomson engine. The standalone moment helper is supplementary and descriptive; it does not itself infer Te, ne or a unique electron velocity distribution.

note: The registered entry performs canonical physical inference from calibrated measured spectra. The separate descriptive moment helper reports wavelength-distribution statistics only; it is not a velocity distribution or independent ne/Te estimator.

limitations: Calibration coefficient and signal units must be documented and valid over the sampled range and bandwidth.

Drift correction assumes the true signal is approximately zero in both selected windows.

quantities: ψ(R,Z), magnetic axis, separatrix, X-point, q(r), κ, δ, β_p, l_i
method: Prescribed-boundary Grad–Shafranov solve; weighted inverse flux-basis fit to calibrated magnetic probes and/or flux loops; joint flux-bin source decomposition of p'(psi) and F F'(psi) using R² variation; integrated pressure relative to zero edge pressure; derived toroidal current-density map; optional F(psi) and q(psi) using supplied edge F=R Bphi. The prescribed-profile solver now exports pressure-relative-to-edge, source profiles, and toroidal-current density derived directly from the same supplied source functions; an independent edge F constraint may be supplied to integrate F(psi).
caveat: Generic EFIT-like toolkit, not a complete machine-specific free-boundary EFIT. Pressure/current source decomposition from psi alone is not unique when the per-flux-bin R² design is rank-deficient; the result reports identifiability. Absolute pressure assumes p(edge)=0. q(r) requires an independently supplied edge F=R Bphi value and valid closed flux contours. Geometry, calibration, coil responses, uncertainties, and diagnostic constraints must be supplied and validated.
implementation_status: Implemented scoped prescribed-boundary Grad–Shafranov solve, direct derivation/export of pressure and toroidal-current profiles from the exact supplied p'(psi_N) and F F'(psi_N) source functions, optional F(psi) integration from an independently supplied edge F, and weighted inverse flux-basis fit to calibrated magnetic measurements. Numerical and Streamlit dashboard acceptance tests cover both paths, profile downloads, invalid inputs, identifiability, residual reporting, and downloads. This remains a generic constrained reconstruction workflow, not a complete machine-specific free-boundary EFIT; q and topology-dependent quantities are only reported where independently constrained and numerically supported. The inverse-fit path now propagates supplied measurement uncertainties to coefficient covariance and pointwise flux uncertainty and exports the uncertainty grid; this is conditional uncertainty only, not a full systematic/model uncertainty budget.

limitations: Not a full EFIT implementation or experimental equilibrium inference.

Inverse basis fitting is linearized and cannot replace nonlinear machine-specific EFIT constraints or a Grad–Shafranov-consistent profile inversion.
Inverse-fit uncertainty is conditional on supplied 1-sigma measurement errors and exact response/basis matrices; it is not a total equilibrium uncertainty budget.

execution_contract.algorithm: Compute the multi-species longitudinal dielectric spectral density and infer plasma parameters using differential-evolution or adaptive real-coded genetic global initialization followed by bounded least squares. The regularized option adds a scaled prior penalty; infer_tabulated_1d adds a non-negative softmax VDF parameterization and second-difference smoothness penalty. Full spectral covariance whitening, response/external Monte Carlo and residual-based model-discrepancy diagnostics are available.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Local Jacobian covariance with optional full spectral covariance whitening. Supplied instrument-response uncertainty and supported probe-frequency, scattering-angle (scalar geometry), electron-flow and ion-fraction uncertainties are propagated by Monte Carlo refits. Excess reduced chi-square above unity is reported as a separate model-discrepancy covariance component. Inferred tabulated fast-ion VDF logit covariance is transformed to VDF-node covariance. Ion-fraction uncertainties are independently perturbed and renormalized; full species-composition covariance is not supported.
limitations: Not a full magnetized electromagnetic CTS scattering tensor, ray-tracing/beam-overlap model or receiver/absolute-power transfer model.
Ion composition is fixed externally; uncertainty can be supplied for charge-density fractions but the species identities are not inferred.
The adaptive real-coded genetic option is an independent implementation informed by Zhang et al. (2024), not a claim of exact reproduction of their article-specific fitness function.

A tabulated fast-ion VDF is a 1-D projected distribution. Its reconstruction is ill-posed and depends on velocity grid, initial distribution and regularization strength; it is not a unique unrestricted 3-D VDF measurement.
The hot-Maxwellian option remains a two-population parameterization.
The electrostatic longitudinal susceptibility omits magnetized electromagnetic tensor response, ray tracing, polarization coupling, beam overlap and absolute received-power calibration.
Model-discrepancy covariance is a residual-based conditional diagnostic, not independent experimental validation.
One common ion temperature and one common projected ion flow are shared across all background ion species; species-specific Ti and flow inference is not implemented.
Electron-flow projection must be supplied explicitly; zero is accepted only as an intentional stationary-flow assumption.
Full covariance/correlation matrix for ion-composition fractions is not accepted; supplied per-species fraction uncertainties are perturbed independently and renormalized.

assumptions: Input spectra and wavelength axes are measured and calibrated; calibration is not performed by Analysis 1.
Spatial coordinates are supplied for each measured channel.
Non-collective Maxwellian model assumes isotropic non-relativistic Maxwellian electrons.
Collective Maxwellian model requires explicit ion species and ion temperatures; missing values are not silently inferred.
Absolute density requires W/nm spectral intensity and complete optical geometry/polarization inputs.
Collective-mode flow vectors and incident/scattered beam directions are expressed in one explicitly supplied coordinate frame; no canonical beam orientation is assumed.
preprocessing: Validate finite channel-by-wavelength arrays, channel-to-radius correspondence and strictly increasing calibrated wavelength axes without sorting, repairing or dropping source samples.

Apply the supplied instrument response in bin-integrated spectral-power space using calibrated wavelength-bin widths, then convert back to spectral density; 1-D index kernels require a uniform wavelength grid.
execution_contract.algorithm: Forward-fit measured multi-channel Thomson spectra with the supplied instrument response. Infer per-channel electron temperature and supported flow projection; infer collective-mode density only where the collective spectral shape resolves it, and non-collective absolute density only when calibrated spectral power and complete optical geometry are supplied.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Non-collective fits use local fit covariance and optional Monte Carlo LSF uncertainty. A full channel-major covariance is handled by joint GLS for Maxwellian/Kappa and final physical parameters, integrated powers and absolute densities are recomputed from the joint fit. Collective external-parameter Monte Carlo includes supplied ion-temperature, ion/electron flow-vector, laser-wavelength, scattering-angle or beam-direction component, and measured response-matrix uncertainties; the returned covariance includes channel density, temperature and projected flow parameters. A supplied 6x6 relative optical-input covariance is authoritative and mutually exclusive with separate scalar uncertainty inputs. Excess reduced chi-square is exposed as a separate model-adequacy covariance diagnostic, not experimental validation. Optional joint_density_relative_covariance provides a complete 6N x 6N channel-major covariance for absolute-density inversion and returns the full cross-channel density covariance; it cannot be combined with joint_spectral_covariance or separate response/scalar optical uncertainty models.
limitations: Full 3-D relativistic photon-geometry integration is not implemented; the relativistic option uses a 1-D projected Maxwell-Juttner approximation.
Collective non-Maxwellian kinetic distributions are not implemented; the collective backend is Maxwellian.
The kappa model is a parameterized isotropic non-Maxwellian approximation, not arbitrary VDF inversion.
Absolute density is not identifiable from spectral shape alone.
No independent experimental validation is claimed.
Collective multi-species inference requires explicit ion composition fractions; ion temperatures and flow vectors must be supplied or stationary assumptions declared.
Collective-mode fitting requires explicit incident/scattered beam direction vectors consistent with the supplied scattering angle.
Joint full-covariance GLS is currently implemented for non-collective Maxwellian and Kappa projected spectra; other models require dedicated joint forward models.
Model-discrepancy covariance uses excess reduced chi-square as a conditional diagnostic and is not a substitute for independent model validation.

Collective beam-direction component uncertainties are propagated as independent component-wise Gaussian perturbations; correlations among beam-vector components and correlations with other external inputs are not represented.
A supplied density_relative_covariance is authoritative for all six optical inversion inputs, including the scattered-power uncertainty; do not also supply separate scalar uncertainties.
